summary: Turkish Aerospace / TUM authors compare five RAG pipelines (dense top-k, an agentic LangGraph loop, agentic plus a typed-graph tool, a typed-edge graph walk they call GraphRAG, and a rule or learned router) on a synthetic 1,132-requirement DO-178C-style trace corpus (296 hop-stratified queries x 3 seeds x 2 embedders) and a 200-query MuSiQue subset. Answers are scored by citation F1 against gold requirement IDs, and faithfulness by GPT-5.4 and GPT-4.1 judges. The graph walk ties dense retrieval on 1-2-hop trace questions and leads on 3+-hop (significant only with the local embedder), but 3+-hop citation F1 never exceeds 0.25 on requirements; the LLM judges disagree with each other and with themselves over time (same-input re-judge after 11 weeks: kappa 0.14 and -0.05).

claims.claim: Scoring the retrieved set instead of the answer's citations inverts the architecture ranking (GraphRAG context precision 0.12-0.23 vs citation precision 0.48-0.65)
claims.evidence: Table 2 top block across v2, v3 and MuSiQue: 11-15 context IDs at 0.120/0.129/0.227 precision vs 3.4-5.0 cited IDs at 0.480/0.493/0.654. The inversion follows directly from the reported numbers; it is a measurement-point effect that holds in all three settings.

claims.claim: Answer-level winners are corpus- and stratum-conditional but embedder-robust; agentic pipelines lead only on 3+-hop requirement queries
claims.evidence: Table 1: vanilla and GraphRAG tie on 1-2-hop DO-178C (Wilcoxon p=0.12/0.65); on 3+-hop the local embedder gives agentic-graph 0.219 vs vanilla 0.089 (Holm p<1e-6), but under the Azure embedder no 3+-hop pair passes the joint significance criterion and GraphRAG 0.253, adaptive 0.254 and agentic-graph 0.251 are tied. C1 is not replicated cross-corpus for the agentic arms (MuSiQue ran only three pipelines).

claims.claim: On DO-178C, faithfulness declines with hop distance (trend p<0.05 in three of four judge x embedder combinations); on Wikipedia it does not collapse
claims.evidence: Table 2 C2b and Cochran-Armitage tests. The 11-week replication batch reproduces the decline under GPT-5.4 only, while GPT-4.1 then rates 93-95% of everything faithful; which judge carries the trend swaps with the judging date. No human faithfulness labels exist, so the trend rests on judges the paper itself shows are unstable.

claims.claim: Single-judge LLM faithfulness is fragile to retrieval state: GPT-5.4 self-kappa across embedders is 0.137 vs a same-day test-retest floor of 0.76; re-judging frozen inputs 11 weeks later gives kappa <= 0.14 for both judges
claims.evidence: Table 3 same-judge controls on 300 paired tuples. The embedder-swap figure is confounded: the swap changed retrieved contexts and answers on 94% of tuples, so it measures output change plus judge response, as the authors concede. The frozen-input 11-week re-judge (kappa 0.138 GPT-5.4; -0.05/-0.00 GPT-4.1, binomial p<1e-44 against stationarity) is the clean evidence for judge drift.

claims.claim: A learned router on dense embeddings alone reaches macro-F1 0.86 on hop classification
claims.evidence: Table 4: 50-fold CV 0.78±0.08 (local) and 0.86±0.05 (Azure). The queries are LLM-generated, the per-stratum routing target is derived once from the full matrix rather than per fold, and the authors say transfer to human-authored queries is untested.

patterns.note: Isolating comparison (same generator, prompt and embedder; only retrieval differs): a typed-edge graph walk ties dense top-k on 1-2-hop trace questions and leads on 3+-hop (significant only with the local embedder), and wins every MuSiQue stratum even with distractor edges added. But it floods the context (precision 0.12-0.23), and on the requirements corpus faithfulness falls with hop count, which the authors attribute to expansion pulling in contradicting cross-module requirements.
Dense top-k is co-best on 1-2-hop trace questions (F1 0.69-0.76) and worst or near-worst on 3+-hop (0.09-0.20). No lexical/BM25 or reranker baseline was run.

Pipelines answer trace-chain questions over an explicit typed link store (derives_from/satisfies/traces_to), with cited IDs checked against gold IDs. Using the verified links (graph arms) helps multi-hop recall vs dense retrieval, but 3+-hop citation F1 stays <= 0.25 on requirements in every pipeline: LLM-assembled multi-hop trace answers are mostly wrong unless each cited link is checked against the store. Links are requirement-to-requirement/verification, not to code.

Direct evidence against relying on a single LLM judge across time or pipeline changes: same-input re-judging 11 weeks apart gives kappa 0.14 (GPT-5.4) and about 0 (GPT-4.1, +41 pp leniency shift) vs a same-day floor of 0.76; inter-judge kappa is 0.02 on MuSiQue. No human labels, so which judge is right is unknown.

methodology.sample: Synthetic DO-178C-style corpus (1,132 requirements, 32 modules, generated by GPT-5.4 from a hand-authored taxonomy); 296 hop-stratified queries x 5 pipelines x 3 seeds x 2 embedders = 8,880 runs; MuSiQue 200 queries x 3 pipelines x 1 seed plus a 200-run distractor-edge control; >5,000 faithfulness judgments on paired 300-tuple subsets
methodology.baselines: Dense top-k vanilla RAG; no BM25/lexical baseline, no cross-encoder reranker, and none of the cited traceability systems (LiSSA, TVR) run; 'GraphRAG' is a local typed-edge walk, not Edge et al.'s community-summary system
methodology.models: GPT-5.4 (2026-03-05) generator and judge; GPT-4.1 judge and a 332-row generator-swap control; embedders multilingual-e5-small and text-embedding-3-small
methodology.variance: 3 seeds; paired BCa bootstrap CIs, Holm-corrected Wilcoxon with Cliff's delta threshold; Wilson CIs and trend tests for faithfulness; per-stratum n 95-111
methodology.ablations: Embedder swap, corpus swap, judge pairing, generator swap, distractor-edge control; rule vs learned router
methodology.contamination_controls: Corpus is synthetic but generated by the same model family that answers and judges (circular rather than clean); MuSiQue is public
methodology.languages: Natural-language requirements and Wikipedia paragraphs; no code

standards.peer_review: Not stated; 6-page short-paper format, journal extension mentioned
standards.artifacts: Corpus described as publicly released and the pipeline as regenerable from one make target, but the paper gives no URL; no code link found

biases.detail: The DO-178C corpus was generated by GPT-5.4, which also generates answers and judges faithfulness; the authors acknowledge the corpus-author leg of the circularity remains.
Faithfulness has no human reference labels; the paper's own controls show the two judges disagree (kappa 0.02 on MuSiQue) and drift over 11 weeks.
One generator family (GPT-5.4, with a GPT-4.1 swap on 332 rows); both judges from the same vendor.
Faithfulness is judged against the full retrieved block, so pipelines that flood the context are penalised for material their answer did not cite (§6).
Release is claimed but no link is provided in the paper.

coi.affiliations: Turkish Aerospace Industries (3 authors); Technical University of Munich (corresponding author)
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Azure OpenAI models and embeddings used as components; no author product evaluated
coi.detail: No commercial interest in any pipeline or model compared.

verdict_reason: Careful statistics (3 seeds, paired bootstrap, Holm correction, test-retest and 11-week judge controls) and an honest threats section. Caveats: synthetic corpus written by the same model family that answers and judges, no human faithfulness labels, one generator family, no lexical baseline, and no artifact link. The judge-drift result and the measurement-point inversion are the robust takeaways; the per-stratum winner claims are partly non-significant under the second embedder.
applicability: Two things transfer to a discovery and traceability harness across the team's several repositories. First, if the team keeps a requirement/spec-to-code link store (P42), answer trace questions by walking explicit typed links, and check every ID the model cites against the store: even with graph help, 3+-hop answers here were mostly wrong (citation F1 <= 0.25). Second, do not use one LLM judge's score as a regression gate across weeks or retrieval changes. Pin the judge snapshot, measure same-day test-retest agreement first, and keep a small human-labelled set to re-anchor it. The aerospace corpus is synthetic, so the absolute numbers do not transfer.

conflicts_with.detail: That study validates a Claude Sonnet 4.6 judge against three blind engineers (kappa 0.74) and treats it as a reliable proxy, while this paper shows GPT-5.4/GPT-4.1 judges agree with their own earlier verdicts only at kappa 0.14 / ~0 after 11 weeks. The tasks differ (graded QA rubric vs binary faithfulness), so judge validity has to be re-established per task and per date, not assumed.
